Placing a rung there would mean inventing a correspondence the curriculum does not state.

disputedByLadder.claim: PU.direct-address has no place on the ladder, because Alberta never names the comma before or after a name being addressed.
disputedByLadder.ladderFinds: Alberta names no K–4 outcome for it, which is true, but Grade 5 and Grade 6 both state "Apply punctuation to support effective written communication" (conventions.grade5.02, conventions.grade6.02). That covers it, so the skill has a place — at grade, not below it.
disputedByLadder.effect: Moved from "no curriculum basis" to a Grade 5 rung. The distinction matters to a child: no specific K–4 outcome is not the same as no outcome at all.

disputedByLadder.claim: PH.blend-segment, PH.vowels, PH.digraphs-clusters, PH.syllables and PH.multisyllable have no Grade 5/6 outcome because "Alberta ends the Phonics organizing idea after Grade 4".
disputedByLadder.ladderFinds: Alberta ends Phonics after Grade 3, not Grade 4. Page 33 heads the Grade 3/Grade 4 spread but prints one set of columns, and the Grade 4 half of that table does not exist. Phonological Awareness ends after Grade 2 and Fluency after Grade 4.
disputedByLadder.effect: The conclusion (no Grade 5/6 outcome) is unchanged. The stated reason is off by one grade.

disputedByLadder.claim: GR.reflexives, GR.relative, GR.interrogative, GR.demonstrative and GR.indefinite have no Grade 5/6 outcome.
disputedByLadder.ladderFinds: Grade 5 Conventions states "Distinguish between different types of pronouns used in a sentence" (conventions.grade5.11). It names the class without listing which types, so all five sit under one outcome — which is not the same as having none.
disputedByLadder.effect: Whether one outcome naming no types is evidence for five separate skills is a judgement for the parent. The ladder places them at Grade 5 and flags it here rather than deciding quietly.
